textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a CELL MEMBRANE (plasma membrane) shown as a CUTAWAY SLAB seen edge-on — a rectangular cross-section band running horizontally, filling most of the square frame — centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space so labels can attach later. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark-charcoal background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. STRUCTURE, read top to bottom: a TOP ROW of round teal-blue phospholipid HEADS (the outer leaflet, facing the extracellular space above the slab), then a band of pale warm-gold, string-like TAILS hanging DOWN from those heads, then — meeting them from below — a mirrored second set of gold TAILS pointing UP, topped by a BOTTOM ROW of the same round teal-blue HEADS (the inner leaflet, facing the cytoplasm below the slab). The two rows of tails MUST meet and mingle in the exact middle of the slab — this tails-together, heads-apart arrangement is the single most important thing to get right; never reverse it. Through this bilayer, embedded and crossing its FULL thickness top to bottom, place at least one brick-red INTEGRAL/TRANSMEMBRANE PROTEIN shaped so a visible pale CHANNEL/PORE runs straight through its centre from the top face to the bottom face. Elsewhere, place a soft-green PERIPHERAL PROTEIN resting on top of the outer row of heads only (not sunk into the tails, not on the inner face). Wedge two or three small dusty-violet CHOLESTEROL shapes in among the tail band, parallel to the tails. From the top (outer) row ONLY, draw two or three branching golden-yellow sugar-chain shapes (the GLYCOCALYX) projecting upward into the extracellular space above the slab — do NOT draw any sugar chains hanging from the bottom row. The heads should be densely but irregularly packed — like a soft mosaic, not a rigid engineered grid — to read as fluid, not solid. CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC RULES: it is always a BILAYER (two rows of heads), never a single layer; tails always point INWARD toward each other, heads always point OUTWARD into the two watery spaces; the glycocalyx sugar chains appear ONLY on the top/outer row, never the bottom/inner row; the integral protein spans the full slab thickness with a visible pore; the peripheral protein touches only one face; nothing looks like a rigid brick wall or crystal lattice; no ribosomes anywhere; no bacterial or plant cell wall outside the slab. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.

Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks anywhere in the image.
